challenges.name: context-window-quiz
challenges.title: What fits, and what the trim removed
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the tutor incident: the API error for a long chat, and the trimming loop that was proposed as a fix.

questions.explanation: True. The context window is one budget for input and output together: 7650 tokens of messages plus 500 requested for the answer is 8150, which is within 8192. That shows how the window is counted, but it is only a stopgap: the answer now has half the room, and the next turn adds more messages, so the chat fails again a turn or two later. The lasting fix is to trim the history to a budget of window minus reserved output. The misconception is that the context window limits only what you send, so the output limit could not matter.

False. The system prompt is the first element of the array, and shift() removes the first element, so it is the very first thing this loop drops when the chat is too long. From then on every request reaches the model without the rules, and the model has no memory of them from earlier requests. Keep the system prompt outside the part you trim (or always put it back first) and trim only the history, oldest first. The misconception is that being first in the array makes a message safe; with front-trimming it makes it the first to go.

challenges.name: fit-chat-into-context
challenges.title: Trim a chat to fit the context window
challenges.description: CodeDev's AI tutor resends the whole chat on every turn. Long chats failed with context_length_exceeded, and a hotfix that kept the last 20 entries cut the system prompt, so the tutor stopped following its rules. Write fitContext(req). The budget for the input is req.contextLimit - req.reservedOutputTokens. Always send the system prompt and the newest message (the last one in req.history); if those two alone need more than the budget, return { error: "does_not_fit" }. Then walk the older messages from newest to oldest and keep each one while the total stays within the budget (total <= budget); stop at the first message that does not fit, and drop it and every older message. Never split a message. Return { sent, dropped, inputTokens }: sent = the system prompt id followed by the kept message ids in chronological order, dropped = the dropped ids in chronological order, inputTokens = the sum of the tokens sent. Before anything else, return { error: "invalid_input" } when contextLimit, reservedOutputTokens, system.tokens or any message's tokens is not a whole number >= 0, when reservedOutputTokens >= contextLimit, or when history is empty or its last message does not have role "user". Token counts are precomputed per message. The test runner reads { requests } as JSON and prints the plan for each request.
hints: Which two messages are in every request no matter what, and how many tokens are left for everything else once you have also set aside the room for the answer?

Look at the loop over the older messages: it should start just before the newest message and move towards index 0, and it should end for good the first time a message would push the total over the budget. Also look at how you build sent: the order you visit messages in is not the order you send them in.

A similar task on a reading list: a learner has 50 minutes, the first video (12 min) is mandatory and so is the most recent one (15 min); the others, oldest to newest, are 10, 20, 5 and 8 min. Left: 50 - 12 - 15 = 23. Walking back from the most recent: 8 fits (15 left), 5 fits (10 left), 20 does not fit, so the walk stops and the 10-minute video is skipped too, even though it would fit. Watch order: 12, 5, 8, 15.

tests.name: A short chat fits: everything is sent, nothing is dropped
The incident: a long tutoring chat keeps the system prompt and drops the oldest turns
The walk stops at the first message that does not fit: smaller older ones are dropped too
Exact fit: a message landing exactly on the budget is kept, and reserved output tokens count
System prompt plus the new question: over budget is does_not_fit, exactly at budget sends only them
Invalid input: empty history, assistant last, negative or fractional tokens, reserve >= limit
Large chat: 2001 messages against a 128k context with 8k reserved for the answer
